 UK egg producer trials acoustic technology to monitor hen welfare
 

 Noble Foods and AgriSound test sound-based system on free-range farms

 

 
 
 
 
 26 August 2026
 
 

 
 
 
 5 minute read
 
 

 
 
 
 By: Global Ag Media 
 

 

 
 
 
 
 Europe

 

 

 

 

 Noble Foods has launched a pioneering on‑farm project to explore how acoustic technology can be used to better understand, monitor and improve the welfare of laying hens – marking a significant leap forward in evidence‑led animal welfare in UK egg production, according to a company-issued press release. 

The project was made possible through a successful funding bid to Innovate UK, the UK’s national innovation agency, led by Emily Marshall, Agriculture Sustainability Manager at Noble Foods. The funding supports a two‑year research‑led trial designed to test how emerging agri‑tech can be applied practically, credibly and at scale within a commercial laying hen environment.

Developed in partnership with agri‑tech specialists AgriSound and Aviasenze, and hosted on a working free‑range farm in East Yorkshire, the project will trial a new acoustic welfare monitoring system designed specifically for laying hens – the first application of its kind within the UK egg sector.

Alongside the free-range trial, Noble Foods is also testing the technology within one of its barn laying facilities. Evaluating the system across both housing environments will help determine how acoustic monitoring can be used to better understand bird welfare in different settings, providing valuable insight into flock behaviour, environmental influences and welfare indicators. The aim is to ensure the learning generated by the project is relevant to a broad cross-section of UK egg production.

This marks the second collaboration between Noble Foods and AgriSound, following an earlier pilot that saw Noble become the first UK egg producer to trial bioacoustic pollinator monitoring on farm. Insights from that project helped inform how sound‑based data could be applied more broadly within agricultural systems, including its potential to support animal welfare.

The technology analyses the soundscape within poultry houses, using machine learning to identify patterns in flock vocalisations and activity that may indicate changes in behaviour, health or environmental conditions. The aim is to provide farm teams with earlier, data‑led insight that can support proactive welfare management alongside traditional stockmanship.

“This project demonstrates how AgriSound’s expertise in bioacoustics AI can be applied beyond pollinators to help address some of the most important challenges in animal agriculture”, said Casey Woodward, CEO, Agrisound.

“We are excited to support Noble Foods and Aviasenze in developing new welfare-monitoring algorithms that have the potential to improve the health and wellbeing of laying hens at scale”, says Casey Woodward, CEO, AgriSound.

Animal welfare in egg production has traditionally been measured through a combination of standards, audits and assurance schemes. These important mechanisms provide confidence and accountability but often offer only periodic snapshots of life on farm.

“Chicken welfare is not only an ethical responsibility but a crucial driver of productivity. Even small improvements to egg production results in substantial benefits to a farmer’s bottom line and UK food security. Aviasenze automated monitoring technology enables farmers to rapidly identify and respond to problems in the flock before they escalate. We are excited to demonstrate how Aviasenze can support the future of layer-hen welfare and more efficient egg production”, says Heather Sanders, of Aviasenze.

This project seeks to explore how welfare monitoring can evolve further, by introducing continuous, non‑invasive insight drawn directly from the birds themselves. By listening to flock behaviour in real time, the partners hope to better understand how changes in environment, management or health may manifest before issues escalate.

Within the project team, the technology has earned the nickname ‘Happy-o-Meter’ due to its focus on helping farmers better understand indicators of bird wellbeing. While the trial is firmly rooted in science and evidence gathering, the informal name reflects the ambition to listen more closely to hens and learn what their behaviour may tell us about their welfare.

“There is growing interest – and scrutiny – around how we talk about hen welfare, and rightly so. This project is about going beyond assurance alone and exploring how emerging science can give us deeper, more continuous insight into the lived experience of the bird, whether that’s within a free-range or barn environment,” says Emily Marshall, Agriculture Sustainability Manager, Noble Foods.

“By listening to hens and understanding how changes in sound and behaviour might indicate shifts in welfare or environment, we can support farmers with earlier, more confident decision‑making. This is not about replacing good stockmanship but complementing it with better data. We see this as a learning project for the wider sector. If we are going to build trust and move the welfare conversation forward, we need to be open to testing new approaches, sharing the evidence and being honest about what works – and what still needs to improve.”

The trial is being hosted by free-range farmer Will Waind, a Happy Egg producer who recently re‑entered egg production and is actively engaged in testing new approaches that can strengthen welfare and farm resilience. Rather than operating in a controlled test environment, the system is being trialled within the realities of a working commercial farm – ensuring that any insights are grounded in day‑to‑day practice and producer needs.

“As a farmer, your job is to spot small changes before they become big problems, but you can’t be everywhere at once. What appealed to me about this project is the idea of having another set of ‘ears’ in the shed, picking up on things that might otherwise be missed.” 

“We’ve all been through a tough few years in egg production, from bird flu to rising costs, so any innovation must be genuinely practical and work in the real world. This trial isn’t about replacing our work – it’s about giving us better tools to support welfare and make confident decisions. If testing new approaches like this helps improve outcomes for hens and gives farmers more confidence in how they manage their flocks, then it’s worth being involved. Progress only happens if someone’s willing to try it on farm.”

Noble Foods is clear that the project is not positioned as a finished solution or a single answer to welfare challenges, but as a learning‑led trial designed to generate evidence, test assumptions and inform future thinking.

By working alongside technology partners, farmers and Innovate UK, the company says it hopes the outcomes will help shape broader conversations around welfare monitoring, agri‑tech adoption and transparency across the UK egg industry.

Findings from the trial will be reviewed over the two‑year period and shared with producers and industry stakeholders, helping identify where acoustic monitoring can add value and where further development is needed.

translationZh:
Noble Foods启动了一项开创性的农场项目，探索如何利用声学技术更好地理解、监测和改善蛋鸡福利——据公司发布的新闻稿称，这标志着英国鸡蛋生产在循证动物福利方面迈出了重要一步。

该项目通过向英国国家创新机构Innovate UK成功申请资金得以实现，由Noble Foods农业可持续发展经理Emily Marshall牵头。资金支持一项为期两年的研究性试验，旨在测试新兴农业技术如何在商业化蛋鸡养殖环境中实际、可信且规模化地应用。

该项目与农业技术专家AgriSound和Aviasenze合作开发，并在东约克郡一个正在运营的自由放养农场进行，将试验一种专为蛋鸡设计的声学福利监测系统——这是英国蛋鸡行业的首次此类应用。

除了自由放养试验外，Noble Foods还在其一个棚舍蛋鸡设施中测试该技术。在这两种养殖环境中评估该系统，将有助于确定声学监测如何在不同环境中更好地理解鸡只福利，为鸡群行为、环境影响和福利指标提供宝贵见解。目标是确保项目产生的知识适用于英国鸡蛋生产的广泛领域。

这是Noble Foods与AgriSound的第二次合作，此前的一次试点使Noble成为英国首家在农场试验生物声学传粉媒介监测的蛋鸡生产商。该项目的见解有助于了解基于声音的数据如何在农业系统中更广泛应用，包括其支持动物福利的潜力。

该技术分析禽舍内的声景，利用机器学习识别鸡群发声和活动中的模式，这些模式可能表明行为、健康或环境条件的变化。目的是为农场团队提供更早、基于数据的洞察，以支持主动福利管理，补充传统养殖技术。

“这个项目展示了AgriSound在生物声学AI方面的专业知识如何超越传粉媒介，帮助解决动物农业中一些最重要的挑战，”AgriSound首席执行官Casey Woodward说。

“我们很高兴支持Noble Foods和Aviasenze开发新的福利监测算法，这些算法有潜力大规模改善蛋鸡的健康和福祉，”AgriSound首席执行官Casey Woodward说。

鸡蛋生产中的动物福利传统上通过标准、审计和保证计划的组合来衡量。这些重要机制提供了信心和问责制，但往往只提供农场生活的周期性快照。

“鸡只福利不仅是道德责任，也是生产力的关键驱动力。即使鸡蛋生产的小幅改善也能为农民带来可观的经济效益和英国粮食安全。Aviasenze的自动化监测技术使农民能够快速识别并响应鸡群中的问题，防止其升级。我们很高兴展示Aviasenze如何支持蛋鸡福利的未来和更高效的鸡蛋生产，”Aviasenze的Heather Sanders说。

该项目旨在探索福利监测如何进一步发展，通过引入直接从鸡只本身获得的连续、非侵入性洞察。通过实时聆听鸡群行为，合作伙伴希望更好地理解环境、管理或健康的变化如何在问题升级之前显现。

在项目团队中，该技术因其专注于帮助农民更好地理解鸡只福祉指标而获得了“快乐计”的绰号。虽然试验牢牢植根于科学和证据收集，但这个非正式名称反映了更贴近母鸡、了解它们的行为可能告诉我们什么关于其福利的雄心。

“人们对如何谈论母鸡福利的兴趣和审视日益增加，这是理所当然的。这个项目旨在超越单纯的保证，探索新兴科学如何给我们提供更深入、更持续的洞察，了解鸡只的实际体验，无论是在自由放养还是棚舍环境中，”Noble Foods农业可持续发展经理Emily Marshall说。

“通过聆听母鸡，理解声音和行为的变化如何可能表明福利或环境的转变，我们可以支持农民做出更早、更自信的决策。这不是要取代良好的养殖技术，而是用更好的数据补充它。我们认为这是整个行业的学习项目。如果我们要建立信任并推动福利对话向前发展，我们需要开放地测试新方法，分享证据，并诚实地面对什么有效——以及什么仍需改进。”

该试验由自由放养农场主Will Waind主持，他是Happy Egg的生产商，最近重新进入鸡蛋生产，并积极参与测试可以加强福利和农场韧性的新方法。该系统不是在受控的测试环境中运行，而是在一个运营中的商业农场内进行试验——确保任何见解都基于日常实践和生产者的需求。

“作为农民，你的工作是及早发现小变化，防止它们变成大问题，但你不可能无处不在。这个项目吸引我的地方在于，在鸡舍里有另一双‘耳朵’，捕捉可能被忽略的事情。”

“我们都经历了鸡蛋生产的艰难几年，从禽流感到成本上升，所以任何创新都必须真正实用，并在现实世界中有效。这个试验不是要取代我们的工作——而是给我们更好的工具来支持福利并做出自信的决策。如果像这样测试新方法有助于改善母鸡的福利，并给农民更多管理鸡群的信心，那么参与是值得的。进步只有有人愿意在农场尝试才会发生。”

Noble Foods明确表示，该项目不是作为最终解决方案或福利挑战的单一答案，而是作为一项以学习为主导的试验，旨在产生证据、检验假设并为未来思考提供信息。

该公司表示，通过与技术合作伙伴、农民和Innovate UK合作，希望结果将有助于塑造围绕福利监测、农业技术采用和英国鸡蛋行业透明度的更广泛对话。

试验结果将在两年期间进行审查，并与生产者和行业利益相关者分享，帮助确定声学监测在哪些方面可以增加价值，以及哪些方面需要进一步发展。

UK egg producer trials acoustic technology to monitor hen welfare 
Noble Foods and AgriSound test sound-based system on free-range farms
